projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Thomas Verran was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay, this interview is with Thomas Verran, from Emerald Isle, North Carolina. Today is July 22, 2003, and we'll go ahead and get started with you. You, sir, you just want to talk about whether you were drafted, or did you enlist, and just go --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I enlisted. The first time I went in, I enlisted.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: What year was that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: 1945, yeah, the end of '45, and, I went from Detroit, and we went to boot camp, came home for 10 or 12 days, whatever it was, and took off. 18 months later, I came back, and we were on a, I was on a ship that's sort of like a A.P., which was a transport delivery, and they would go to all these different islands and drop things off, pick them up, and stuff like that. But the only excitement that I really seen was, there are a lot of mines out there and they were always shooting at mines.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: This was World War II, the tail end --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: The tail end of World War II.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So, you were just out there looking for mines, or just --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, these -- they was just floating around, a lot of mines --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right there in the water --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Out in the water, and they'd find them, and they'd try to shoot them, and miss half the time, but (laughs), but they did pretty good, but that's -- that's really in the Navy the only excitement I had, it was sort of a boring type of thing.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: What made you stay in?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, in those days, I mean, everybody went in the service, that's, you know, and I had went to a trade school, like Henry Ford trade school, and they was just like a prison. I mean, you went to school one week, and you worked in the factory two weeks, learning your different trades. When I got out of that school, though, I was a good machinist. But, naturally, the Navy didn't put you in to be a machinist. I ended up being, like a deckhand, or something like that, and they wasted -- and that's one reason I was disappointed in it, but -- I don't know, you have to be a different person to enjoy -- I would say, any way.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So when you left the Navy, what happened then?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I went back to Michigan, and I took an apprenticeship -- I was taking apprenticeship in hydraulics, and [ducts] for hydraulics, and then the Korean War broke out, and I joined up in the paratroopers then.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And you did that -- you joined yourself --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, I joined, I joined, I joined.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So you became a paratrooper, and that required more training, or more --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, yes, if you get into the individual floor outfits, like the paratroopers, Marines, things like that, you're better trained than you are just going into the regular infantry, you know, or just in the military. And that's why I went there, and then I went to, oh, and then to Camp Campbell, Kentucky, and that's where we -- I took training in the Fort Benning, and then went to Camp Campbell, stayed there and trained, and then we went to, you know, Korea. When they got to Korea, they were going in, in the -- staying in Japan, see, the 187th that I was in --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: They were stationed in Japan --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: In Japan, okay, but I didn't feel like going to that dress stuff, and shining, and they had -- we had [?a lot of?] opportunity, but you could go to other infantry divisions in -- that were fighting in Korea, so that's how I ended up in the Third Infantry (laughs). Myself and three or four other guys, because I didn't want to shine my boots any more, you know, so we went to Korea.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I joined the Third Infantry Division, yeah, Fifth, yeah, 15th Regiment.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: What was it like when you arrived in Korea, and was it -- was it what you expected?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, first thing when you approach any of those, that, Korea, you could smell it (laughs), like, when you flew over to Japan, and then you got on the ship, and you can actually smell like, the food they eat -- I don't know what it is, but, you could smell Japan -- and it was cold, I mean, it was seriously cold there. Well, then, they put us, you know, broke us up and put us into outfits, and, yeah, well, I remember it was very cold, like sub zero cold --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: -- and then we went -- got assigned this outfit, and I remember the first day I went there. We went on this patrol. And, I mean, it was snowing, and it was sort of getting us familiar with, you know, the people and the environment, and -- I was walking like a point man, and I seen somebody walking -- it was a Chinese guy, I guess, because he passed me and I passed him, and we neither one shot at each other --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Just kept walking --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Just walking, yeah, so -- but anyway, that was the first, and then it was just freezing cold there, I mean, you couldn't believe how cold it was there. And they didn't really have good equipment, you know, like they have now, they got, you know, they never had, like, wool overcoats and wool pants --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: They didn't have any of that.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, they had long -- you'd wear long johns --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: How cold was it? Was it below zero, or was it --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: About 15 below, 20, yeah. I mean, it's seriously cold.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: I can imagine.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Up in the -- you get up in the mountains, that's, you know, where we were. And it just was a miserable -- cold, and then we would go on patrol, and set up ambush -- you know, the typical army stuff.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Was there a lot of combat, a lot of --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Quite a -- quite a bit. There was a lot of -- they were always -- we'd go on patrols a lot, looking for them, but then -- you know, if they had -- then they'd do a -- they had like a line or a front, right, and they had bunkers, we had bunkers. And then they would come up at night, and try --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: But you had time to basically build a defense?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. That's what they did, later on, they stopped moving, and they built a defense. Then they would take a hill, or something like that, and then we'd -- they'd have a hill off there, and we'd have to take the hill from them, and we'd back off of it, and they'd move in again, and they'd take the hill over again --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: It was just a back and forth.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, you'd just -- but, then we would -- always trying to capture prisoners, and -- there was a lot of -- we had a lot of shells coming in at us, all the time, and --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Was there a particular experience that you remember, very -- not vividly, but it's something that, when you think of that time period, you --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: The most, yeah, the one experience, the -- the -- you would -- if somebody was there, say, holding this line, then you would relieve them.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Like -- okay, so, say there's a bunker, they got hand grenades, and stuff like that laying around, and sometimes people would pull the pins, you know, loose, you know, they're sort of ___ about hand grenades, and people would, you know -- I'd remember this one, they'd -- ___ our Koreans went in, because we had the Koreans with us -- went in there, and they're moving them around, and one of these grenades blew up, and, you know, just blew the hell out of the guy. But that was, that was -- and then, you know, snipers shooting at people, and then we got overwhelmed a couple of times when we were there.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: How long were you there for?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Year. One year.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: whole year.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And that was basically in the actual combat element --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. One year.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So I can imagine you probably made a lot of friends during that time?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, but I'll tell you what. I couldn't -- someone asked me the other day, "do you know--?", I said, "I don't remember". I really hardly remember where I actually was, you know, because when they came back, they put us on the ship coming back. And people said, "where were you on there?" (Laughs) I never paid attention.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You were just doing your job.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. It was -- a lot of people knew exactly where you were at, and this and that, you know, so -- I didn't. But then, yeah, we had a lot of good -- you meet a lot of good people in the military.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: I notice you had a purple heart, and a silver -- on the other side, do you want to talk about that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, the purple -- well, yeah, sure, if you want. This is -- what's this here?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: It's the -- Silver Star --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: -- Award. Okay. Would you want to talk about that, or is that just something you want --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, I don't know, let me see --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Looks like you've had several Silver Stars --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, this one here was once we got overrun -- I mean, they came on top of us. And I just -- that's when I was in a -- I just went in that bunker, and they had thrown a grenade in there, and that screwed up my hearing for a few days. But then, yeah, this is -- then, we finally got everybody up off of the rear end, and, everybody we -- I don't know, we had about two truckloads that were Chinese at the end, so -- I mean --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Coming at you.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, no, we killed about that many.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Wow. So, basically, you just --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I mean, we were able to get --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Just amazing.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: -- just get to, like that, quick, quick. Came over with two grenades. Luckily, their grenades didn't work all the time. They had like, Chinese wooden grenades, and they'd throw them, and they wouldn't work. Otherwise, we'd -- I wouldn't be here.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Fortunately.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, fortunately for us.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right, if it didn't work, wow. Okay, all right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: That's ___ the end. This is another time that -- that was exciting there. .

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So, did you capture enemy prisoners?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: No, we didn't capture them. But, what happened is, we went, you know, up this hill to try to capture them --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Uh huh.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: And, uh, they have bunkers, you know, you've heard about them, they dig in, and you dig in there, until they can bomb them, ___+. But, anyway, we went there, and then, I thought I was throwing a grenade in a bunker, but it was an ammunition thing.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: An ammunition stock point, okay.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. Which blew me up in the ___. I did about a one -- three sixty up in the air and landed. Didn't even hardly hurt.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And you had a --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Except my hearing.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And you had a friend that was hurt --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, well, yeah, that --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You went over there in a [bus] --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, naturally you do, you know, that was now the rule that you did. And that's what that --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Purple heart.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You got for the --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: That's, I think, yeah, that was one where I blew up that bunker, and when I first -- getting shot at, and all that stuff like that.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Amazing.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: But, here -- now, that, to me -- on the back of it, the colonel --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay. "I shall always remember the fine job you did in the raid on old ___."?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Now, that was nice.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: That was very nice, it's very nice, very personal.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: And then --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Is that the Carl --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, I don't know which one, because I got two of these. See, I got --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay, the Silver Star --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, then, they put -- they give you a oak leaf cluster.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: As you get more -- as you get more and more -- one or two. Great.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Here's for one of these -- I don't know, there are no Silver Star things --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: I'll definitely make a copy of that, and get everything back to you --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I don't know about this other --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So, what did you do, I mean -- was it -- was it -- during that year, was it constant fighting, or was it --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, what you do if you go up and you stay on the front for, say, a month, and then you come back, and they give you -- take a shower, and drink some beer -- you know, like -- and then you'd move back and forth all the time. You might -- it might be two weeks, or they might put you here, and then if there was a problem there, they'd move you over there, you know. And then, we had -- that was the United Nations then, and then we would have the -- the Foreign Legion might have a position, right? And then, we would relieve them --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And then, just take turns --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, going back and forth, so everybody gets a break.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Now, this was the location of the -- was this the "frozen chosen"?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, that was -- yeah, this was after that.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay, this was after that had already happened. Now, when you were there, did you regret the decision you had made to join and to go over, or was it one of those, you just wanted it to end and get back home?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh, not regret, that's a bad word. I don't think I regretted it, it -- it wasn't what I expected, because it's not like the movies, you know. It's terrible. I mean, it's cold, you're miserable. In the summer, it's hot --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: But --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: How many casualties were there?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: How many American casualties?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh, jeez. It was -- I should have brought that book, I've got to -- in fact, I -- when my dad was here, I was -- brought in a little V.F.W. book, and it had the casualties, and --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Thousands.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Thousands, thousands. More than Vietnam. And they had more P.O.W.s, too.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: How did you find out that you were leaving Korea? Did they just tell you that it was time to go, or was there a -- did you know ahead of time that there was a specific amount of time that you were going to be there?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: What? Oh, in Korea?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Then, you'd say for a year, you went --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You knew it was going to be a year.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: year. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay. And what did you do after you left?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Korea?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Uh huh.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh -- went back to Ford, and finished my apprenticeship, and --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And went from there.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Went from there.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you get out of the service at that time?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, I got out of the service. I was going to stay in.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: But you decided to --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. ___+ they were changing a lot of things, and -- I'd probably have been dead if I stayed in.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Probably would have went back.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: (Laughs) Yeah. No, because I would've -- I was going to -- I had a buddy that didn't end up in the Third Division, and he was training Koreans to drop behind the lines, and, you know, before they had the special forces type of thing, and all that, and I met him in Japan, and he said, well, that's a good -- be a good outfit, but, you'd have to sign up for another year, and I said I don't know if I want to do that.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You'd already been through quite a bit.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You saw a lot. Did you do anything for good luck? Did you have any rituals, or anything?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh, good luck?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Any prayers?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Prayed a lot.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Prayed a lot.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Prayed a lot. I was reading the Bible quite a bit then.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You had a Bible with you?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, somebody -- they gave you a little portable -- little Bibles, you know. We would read that a lot.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you all read it together, or was it more --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: No, more of a personal thing. I don't know, a lot of people -- you know, had lucky charms, and everything, but -- who knows?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Again, you see in the movies a lot of times --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah, yeah, yeah. They even had people count for days, and all that stuff, but --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: How was the chow like?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: The chow?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh -- well, of course, we had C-rations then, so that's what -- when you're in the front lines, you eat C-rations, but, then, if you're in reserve, or whatever you want to call it, you'd have regular hot meals. But, C-rations was probably better than some of the food they cooked (laughs).

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you play any pranks, or any practical jokes, or anything like that, on other people, or just --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh, not really. It was just -- it was really too cold to have, you know --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: It was cold the whole time you were there, huh?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: No, but in the summertime, it was too hot, and in the wintertime, it was --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Too cold.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. It was very, I mean, seriously cold.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you have plenty of supplies?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh, yeah, we did, you know, we had everything we needed, except that you needed water, or something, you had to -- I mean, you'd go down and up the [?hill or?] mountain to get water, and -- they had little kerosene stoves -- we had little stoves, I think.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: But you had to get your own water there on the mountain?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. You know, you have to carry a five gallon -- jerry, you know, those little things you see on a jeep, that's what they put water in, you have to lift that. They're young ones, it doesn't bother you too much.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Yeah, we used to try ___+. Did you have any -- I guess you really didn't have any leave time, did you?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Not while -- the only -- when we captured the -- the prisoners, we got R. and R., they let us go to Japan for -- five days, I think.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: What was that like?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: That was good.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Was it fun?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. That's where I met this buddy of mine I was telling you about --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right, right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: No, it was good, very -- you know.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And you said you don't really keep in touch with anybody from that --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I never have -- no. I -- there's one fellow that was in the -- 187th with me, that lived in Detroit, I kept in touch with him for quite a while, but then -- I got -- I moved, you know, from Michigan, and lost contact with him.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you ever join any veterans' organizations?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I belong to the American Legion of V.F.W.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay, all right. I just spoke to one of those the other day.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: I'm not a real great participant, but I still belong.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you want to talk about your [?life after the?] military, any, or family, or anything like that that you want them to interview?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: My family?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Uh huh.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Hell, there probably ain't nobody left (laughs).

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: I'm sorry to hear that.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. Well, my father was in the army, World War I.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: He was in World War I?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. And then, I had a sister, and that was -- but, not like it's a whole -- whole bunch of, you know, military people.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right. Did you ever -- I know you said you did an apprenticeship. Did you ever take advantage of the G. I. bill, or do anything like that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Oh, I think -- yeah, I did. When I first got out, I wanted to build a car, you know, like a hotrod, and I went to a body school, or something like, auto body school, to learn how to weld, and stuff like that.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So, what do you do now?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, I -- I worked for this hydraulic, you know, apprenticeship, and I became a -- electronic bla, bla, bla and I was a field service rep for [Vickers], which is worldwide, and I traveled all over the place.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: All right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Starting up automated equipment, and stuff like that. And I've been back to Korea twice already. I mean, at this age, ___+

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And what was that like?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: They were very modern, oh, yeah. When I left there, they were -- "go home, Yankee," and all that stuff like that, yeah. They were terrible.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And they're like that now.

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah. But now, they're up to the big bucks, they're, you know, like, going to New York City.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So, everything's about travel --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: -- and making a dollar, huh? Is there anything you wanted to add to the interview --

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: No, I just --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Any thoughts on the foreign situation?

sp.speaker: Thomas Verran
sp.p: Well, I'm just -- glad to be American, that's all. I've been to every country, almost, in the world, traveling for [Vickers], and they can't beat this place.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Is that right?
